mainTopic: When a טמא נזיר's new נזירות begins, the woman whose נזירות was cancelled after טומאה, and a נזיר who vowed in a cemetery
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a נזיר who became טמא. The רבנן learn from the פסוק that his new נזירות starts even before he brings his אשם. רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says it starts only once he brings it. רב חסדא explains a ברייתא about a woman whose husband cancelled her נזירות after she became טמאה: she brings the bird חטאת but not the bird עולה. This follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds the husband uproots the vow. The חטאת is still brought because he follows רבי אלעזר הקפר, who teaches that every נזיר is a sinner for holding back from wine. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a person who became a נזיר in a cemetery. שמואל explains that his days count only after he left and fully purified himself. Even if he then went back in, his נזירות had already taken effect. Finally, עולא limits רבי אליעזר's rule that one day is not enough to count as 'first days': it applies only to someone who vowed while already טמא.

steps.title: The new count starts even before the guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (the view of the רבנן) learns from the פסוק that a טמא נזיר's new count of נזירות begins even if he has not yet brought his אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall consecrate … and he shall bring.' This teaches that even though he has not yet brought his offering, his new נזירות has already started.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. Its first opinion learns from the order of words in the פסוק that the new נזירות starts right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'and he shall consecrate' comes before 'and he shall bring.' So the new count of נזירות begins first, and bringing the אשם is not needed to start it.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall consecrate (start his days of נזירות again)
And he shall bring (the אשם, the guilt-offering)

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall consecrate … and he shall bring,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:12. The dots mean the גמרא skips the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא — הִזִּיר.
phrases.english: even though he has not brought, he has consecrated.
phrases.notes: He has not yet brought his אשם, but his new term of נזירות has already begun.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא נזיר's new נזירות begins even before he brings his אשם.

steps.title: The new count starts only once he brings it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה reads the same פסוק to mean the new נזירות begins only when the אשם is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: 'And he shall consecrate … and he shall bring' means: when does he start his new נזירות? At the time he brings his offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees. He reads the same words as saying the new נזירות starts only once the offering is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the two parts of the פסוק go together: the consecrating happens together with the bringing. So bringing the אשם is part of starting over, not just something extra he owes.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the first view

steps.whatToRemember: The two views argue about whether bringing the אשם is needed for the new נזירות to start. The rest of this section builds on רבי ישמעאל's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
"And he shall consecrate … and he shall bring,"
When has he consecrated? At the time that he has brought.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 1's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new נזירות begins only when the אשם is brought.

steps.title: Who taught the case of the woman whose vow was cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind a ברייתא: a woman became a נזירה and then became טמאה, and afterward her husband cancelled her vow. She brings the bird חטאת but not the bird עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the רבנן taught? A woman vowed to be a נזירה and became טמאה, and after that her husband cancelled her vow. She brings the bird sin-offering, but she does not bring the bird burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks whose opinion it follows. This opens a new line of discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא נזיר normally brings two birds, a חטאת and an עולה. This ברייתא splits them: she brings one and not the other. The גמרא wants to know which view explains that split.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught…?
Cancelled (a husband cancelling his wife's vow)

phrases.english: Who taught this
that the Sages taught:
A woman who vowed to be a nazirite and became impure,
and afterward her husband nullified it for her:
she brings the bird sin-offering,
and she does not bring the bird burnt-offering.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that she brings the bird חטאת but not the bird עולה after her husband cancels her vow.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says this ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה from Step 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is the view of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by connecting the ברייתא to רבי ישמעאל, the תנא from the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the offerings are part of the process of fixing the נזירות. So once the husband cancels it, there is no reason to bring the עולה. For the רבנן, the עולה is more like a gift and she would bring it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is Rabbi Yishmael.
phrases.notes: The same רבי ישמעאל from Step 2, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: Uproot or cut off? Either way it doesn't fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a dilemma. If the husband uproots the vow from the start, she shouldn't bring even the חטאת. If he only cuts it off from now on, she should bring the עולה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds the husband uproots the vow completely, she should not bring the bird sin-offering either. If he holds the husband only cuts it off from now on, she should bring the bird burnt-offering too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. It shows that both possible views of a husband's cancellation clash with the ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Uprooting means she was never a נזירה, so she needs no offering at all, not even the חטאת. Cutting off means she really was a טמאה נזירה, so she needs the full set, including the עולה. Bringing only one of the two seems to fit neither view.

keyTerms.meaning: He uproots it (the vow is cancelled from the very start)
He cuts it off (the vow ends only from now on)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terms. עקר means the vow is erased backward, as if it never existed. גייז means the vow was real until now and only stops from this point on.

phrases.english: What does he hold?
If he holds the husband uproots,
she should not bring the bird sin-offering either.
If he holds the husband severs,
she should bring the bird burnt-offering too!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר בַּעַל מִיעְקָר עָקַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Uprooting should cancel both offerings, and cutting off should require both. A split ruling fits neither view.

steps.title: He holds uprooting, and follows רבי אלעזר הקפר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds the husband uproots the vow. The חטאת is still brought because he follows רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really he holds the husband uproots the vow, and רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma. It picks the 'uproot' side and explains the חטאת through another תנא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the vow is uprooted, the עולה, which belongs to fixing the נזירות, falls away. The חטאת stays because of a separate reason taken from רבי אלעזר הקפר. The גמרא explains that reason in the lines that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeping one side of the dilemma)
A תנא whose view explains the חטאת

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a husband's cancellation can erase a vow backward and still leave a חטאת to bring. That opens the door to רבי אלעזר הקפר's idea, explained next.

phrases.english: Actually, he holds the husband uproots,
and Rabbi Yishmael holds
in accordance with Rabbi Elazar HaKappar.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma and adds a second source to explain what is left over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the vow is uprooted, no offering at all should be brought.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow is uprooted, so no עולה is brought. The חטאת is still brought because רבי ישמעאל follows רבי אלעזר הקפר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר הקפר: a נזיר sins by holding back from wine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר הקפר teaches that a נזיר is called a sinner because he made himself suffer by not drinking wine. This explains why the woman still brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר הקפר says: Why does the פסוק say 'and he shall atone for him, because he sinned regarding the soul'? Against which soul did this person sin? It must be that he made himself suffer by not drinking wine. And we can learn a קל וחומר: if someone who only held back from wine is called a sinner, then someone who holds back from everything is a sinner even more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for Step 6's idea: רבי אלעזר הקפר teaches that becoming a נזיר is itself a kind of sin. The reason is that the נזיר makes himself suffer by not drinking wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the נזיר 'sinned regarding the soul,' but he did not hurt anyone. So רבי אלעזר הקפר reads it as a sin against his own self, because he held back from wine. This is why the woman in the ברייתא brings a חטאת even though her husband uprooted her vow: she still held back from wine.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
Soul or self; here, the person's own body
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the foundation for the answer in Step 6. It is also the classic source that making yourself suffer for no reason is not considered praiseworthy.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרַבִּי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, the esteemed one, says:
phrases.notes: בְּרַבִּי is a title of respect for a great scholar, not his father's name.

phrases.english: What does the verse come to teach when it says
"And he shall atone for him, because he sinned regarding the soul"?
Against which soul did this one sin?
Rather, it is that he made himself suffer by holding back from wine.
And we can learn a kal vachomer:
If this one, who did not make himself suffer
except by holding back from wine, is called a sinner,
then one who makes himself suffer by holding back from everything
how much more so is he a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for Step 6's claim that the חטאת is brought because of רבי אלעזר הקפר's view.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that holding back from wine alone makes a נזיר need a חטאת, even if the נזירות is uprooted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר הקפר reading 'אשר חטא על הנפש' (במדבר 6:11).

steps.title: The פסוק speaks only about a טמא נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוק calling a נזיר a sinner is written about a טמא נזיר, but we are using it to say that every נזיר, even a טהור one, is a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that פסוק is written about a טמא נזיר, and we are saying that even a טהור נזיר is a sinner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר הקפר's reading. The פסוק he used appears in the section about a נזיר who became טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sin is simply holding back from wine, then every נזיר should be called a sinner. So why does the תורה say it only about the טמא נזיר? That makes it look as though the sin is linked to the טומאה, not to the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became impure, for example from a dead body
A pure נזיר who completes his term normally

phrases.english: But this is written about an impure nazirite,
and we are saying it about even a pure nazirite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source reading brought in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר הקפר's use of a פסוק about a טמא נזיר to prove that every נזיר is a sinner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The context of the פסוק limits it to a טמא נזיר, while the derived idea applies to all נזירים.

steps.title: Every נזיר sins, but the טמא נזיר sins twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר holds that even a טהור נזיר is a sinner. The פסוק mentions it by the טמא נזיר because he repeated the sin by having to start over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר הקפר holds that a טהור נזיר is also a sinner. The reason it is written by the טמא נזיר is that he sinned again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר הקפר really does mean every נזיר. The תורה chose to say it in the section about the טמא נזיר because his case shows the sin most strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא נזיר has to restart his count, so he holds back from wine for a second round. His sin is doubled, so the תורה states the label 'sinner' there. That does not mean a טהור נזיר is free of the label.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר הקפר, every נזיר is called a חוטא for holding back from wine. The פסוק says it by the טמא נזיר because his sin is doubled. This is why the woman in the ברייתא brings a חטאת even after her husband uprooted her vow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar holds
that a pure nazirite is also a sinner,
and this is the reason it is written about an impure nazirite:
since he repeated the sin.
phrases.notes: His טומאה makes him start his נזירות over, so he holds back from wine all over again.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר נָזִיר טָהוֹר נָמֵי חוֹטֵא הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the פסוק was placed where it is without limiting the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוק appears by a טמא נזיר, only a טמא נזיר would be called a sinner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every נזיר is a sinner. The טמא נזיר is mentioned because he repeated the sin.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: he left the cemetery and came back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about someone who became a נזיר in a cemetery: if he left and came back in, the days count toward his term.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left and entered again, the days count toward his total.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a new line from the משנה to discuss it. This line sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is speaking about a person who accepted נזירות while standing in a cemetery. While he stays there, his days do not count. The משנה says that if he left and came back in, his days do count.

keyTerms.meaning: The days count toward his total of נזירות days

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא וְנִכְנַס — עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: If he left and entered again, the days count toward his tally.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה about a person who became a נזיר while standing in a cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא וְנִכְנַס עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the woman's חטאת and returns to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who left the cemetery and then reentered has his days counted toward his נזירות.

steps.title: How can just leaving start his נזירות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the משנה says the days count, but he is still טמא after leaving. How can his נזירות start just because he walked out?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches that the days count toward his total. Does נזירות start for him just because he left?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה. Leaving the cemetery alone does not make a person טהור, so why would his days start counting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who was in a cemetery is טמא מת. He needs the seven-day purification before he can count נזירות days. So simply walking out should not be enough to start his count.

phrases.english: It teaches: the days count toward his tally.
Just because he left, does naziriteship take effect on him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן מִשּׁוּם דְּיָצָא חָל עֲלֵיהּ נְזִירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the משנה quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the days count after he left.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving does not remove טומאת מת, so נזירות cannot start just from leaving.

steps.title: שמואל: he left and became fully טהור
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about someone who left, received the sprinkling on the third and seventh days, and immersed. Now he is טהור, so his נזירות begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This is a case where he left, was sprinkled, was sprinkled again, and immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by filling in the case. The person did not just walk out; he also went through the full purification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the sprinkling of the פרה אדומה ashes on the third and seventh days and then immersing, he is טהור. His נזירות can then take effect and his days start counting. The משנה left these details out but assumes them.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; this is a case where
He was sprinkled with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
He did it again (a second sprinkling)

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
This is a case where he left and was sprinkled
and was sprinkled again and immersed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּגוֹן שֶׁיָּצָא וְהִזָּה וְשָׁנָה וְטָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by defining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Merely leaving the cemetery starts the נזירות count.
steps.terutzMaskana: He left and completed the purification, so his נזירות took effect.

steps.title: Why does it depend on going back in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the משנה makes it sound like the days count only if he entered again. If he stayed outside, would they not count?
steps.simpleTranslation: So is it only if he entered again that the days count, but if he did not enter again they do not count?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and finds a strange implication. The words 'and entered' suggest that counting depends on going back into the cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he is טהור, his days should count whether or not he goes back in. Going back in should only make him טמא again. So why would the משנה link the counting to reentering?

keyTerms.meaning: Here: so then? (introducing a strange implication)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נִכְנַס הוּא דְּעוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן,
phrases.english: So is it only if he entered that the days count toward his tally,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִכְנַס אֵין עוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן?!
phrases.english: but if he did not enter, they do not count toward his tally?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נִכְנַס הוּא דְּעוֹלִין לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second difficulty on the wording of the same משנה line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'יצא ונכנס' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It implies that without reentering, the days would not count, which makes no sense once he is טהור.

steps.title: Not only if he left, but even if he went back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is using a 'not only this, but even that' style. Of course the days count if he left; they count even if he then went back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'there is no need to say' style: there is no need to say that the days count if he left, but even if he entered again, the days count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'and entered' is not a requirement. It is the bigger point of the teaching: even if he went back in right after becoming טהור, his נזירות had already taken effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple case is that he left, became טהור, and his days count. The משנה adds the harder case: even if he went straight back into the cemetery, his נזירות had already started, so he is treated as a נזיר who became טמא and must bring the offerings for טומאה. This is the 'לא מיבעיא' style, from the obvious case to the bigger one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is speaking in a 'there is no need to say' style

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'and entered' as a condition for the days to count. The days count from the moment he became טהור; 'entered' is the bigger point, not a requirement.
steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה's case, the person left the cemetery and became fully טהור (שמואל), so his נזירות takes effect and his days count. This is true even if he went right back in, and then he is treated as a נזיר who became טמא.

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':
It is not necessary to say this if he left,
but even if he entered again,
the days count toward his tally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording as a 'לא מיבעיא' structure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reentering the cemetery is a condition for the days to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The days count either way; the משנה mentions reentering to teach that even then, the days count.

steps.title: רב's students ask why he never gave this explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי ask their teacher רב why he did not explain the משנה to them the way שמואל did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: Why did you not explain this to us with these words?
steps.whatsHappening: Two of רב's students ask him why he never taught them the explanation שמואל just gave. This question sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל explained that the משנה is talking about a נזיר who left the cemetery and fully purified himself with sprinkling and immersion. The students seem to feel this was an important point, so they ask why רב left it out when he taught them.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא and a student of רב
An אמורא and a student of רב

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
What is the reason you did not explain to us
with these words?
phrases.notes: 'These words' means שמואל's explanation from step 12: he left, got sprinkled on days three and seven, and immersed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to שמואל's explanation by asking why רב had not taught it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב did not teach his students the explanation that the נזיר had already purified himself.

steps.title: רב thought the explanation was obvious
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that he assumed his students did not need the explanation spelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I said to myself, perhaps you do not need it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב says he left out the explanation because he thought it was obvious. That closes this small side discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is not disagreeing with שמואל. He agrees that the משנה means a נזיר who already became טהור. He simply thought any student would understand that by himself.

keyTerms.meaning: I said, meaning I thought to myself

steps.whatToRemember: Both שמואל and רב agree that the משנה is talking about a נזיר who left the cemetery and fully purified himself. Only then do his days begin to count.

phrases.english: He said to them: I said to myself
perhaps you do not need it.
phrases.notes: He means: I thought it was obvious, so I didn't bother saying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוֹן: אָמֵינָא דִּלְמָא לָא צְרִיכִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב assumed the explanation was obvious and did not need to be said.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the same day does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר from the משנה. If the נזיר goes back in on the very same day, the regular rule does not apply, because the פסוק requires 'first days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Not on that very day. As it says, 'And the first days shall fall away,' which means there must first be real 'first days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, where רבי אליעזר adds a limit. If the נזיר becomes טמא again on the very same day he became pure, it is not treated like normal days that get cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a טמא נזיר says his 'first days' are cancelled. רבי אליעזר learns from this that there must be some real 'first days' of pure נזירות, more than one single day. With only one day, the usual laws of a נזיר who became טמא do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא quoted in the משנה
First days, meaning earlier days of pure נזירות
Shall fall away, meaning they are cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying a single day is cancelled. He is saying the opposite: one day is not enough to count as 'first days' at all.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בּוֹ בְּיוֹם —
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Not on that very day —
phrases.notes: He means: if he went back into the cemetery on the same day he became pure.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And the first days shall fall away' —
until there are first days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בּוֹ בְּיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first part of the משנה, the גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר's opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single day of pure נזירות followed by טומאה on that same day does not count as 'first days' that are cancelled. The פסוק requires real earlier days.

steps.title: עולא limits רבי אליעזר's rule
steps.stepSummary: עולא says רבי אליעזר's rule applies only to someone who took the vow while already טמא. A נזיר who started out טהור and then became טמא loses even one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: רבי אליעזר said this only about a טמא person who vowed to be a נזיר. But a pure נזיר who became טמא, even one day is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains how far רבי אליעזר's rule reaches. It covers only someone who became a נזיר while already טמא, like our case in the cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who vowed while טמא never had any pure נזירות until he purified himself, so one day afterward is not enough to count as 'first days.' A נזיר who started out pure is a regular נזיר, so even one pure day is cancelled when he becomes טמא, and the usual laws apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A טמא person who took a vow of נזירות
A pure נזיר who became טמא

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, רבי אליעזר's need for 'first days' applies only to a person who vowed while טמא. For a נזיר who started out pure and then became טמא, even one day is cancelled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming discussion of how many pure days count as 'first days' and when טומאה cancels them.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not say this
except about a טמא person who vowed to be a nazir,
but a pure nazir who became טמא —
even one day is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא בְּטָמֵא שֶׁנָּזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly which case רבי אליעזר's rule from step 17 covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's requirement of 'first days' applies only to one who vowed while טמא. For a pure נזיר who became טמא, even one day is cancelled.
